Two non-zero vectors are collinear when one is a scalar multiple of the other, i.e. when their corresponding components are proportional.

For \(2\widehat{i} - 3\widehat{j} + 4\widehat{k}\) and \(p\widehat{i} + 6\widehat{j} - 8\widehat{k}\):
\(\dfrac{2}{p} = \dfrac{-3}{6} = \dfrac{4}{-8}\)

The second and third ratios are both \(-\dfrac{1}{2}\), and they agree, so the vectors can indeed be collinear. From the first and second ratios,
\(\dfrac{2}{p} = -\dfrac{1}{2}\)
\(\therefore p = -4\)

**Check:** with \(p = -4\), the second vector is \(-4\widehat{i} + 6\widehat{j} - 8\widehat{k} = -2\left( 2\widehat{i} - 3\widehat{j} + 4\widehat{k} \right)\), a scalar multiple of the first. Hence they are collinear.

**Answer:** \(p = -4\)

Let \(\overrightarrow{a} = \widehat{i} - 2\widehat{j} + \widehat{k}\), \(\overrightarrow{b} = 2\widehat{i} - 5\widehat{j} + p\widehat{k}\), \(\overrightarrow{c} = 5\widehat{i} - 9\widehat{j} + 4\widehat{k}\).

Expanding along the first row:
\(1\left( (-5)(4) - p(-9) \right) - (-2)\left( 2(4) - p(5) \right) + 1\left( 2(-9) - (-5)(5) \right) = 0\)
\(\therefore 1\left( -20 + 9p \right) + 2\left( 8 - 5p \right) + 1\left( -18 + 25 \right) = 0\)
\(\therefore -20 + 9p + 16 - 10p + 7 = 0\)
\(\therefore 3 - p = 0\)
\(\therefore p = 3\)

Writing \(\overrightarrow{c} = m\overrightarrow{a} + n\overrightarrow{b}\) and comparing components gives \(m + 2n = 5\), \(-2m - 5n = -9\), \(m + 3n = 4\); the first and third give \(n = -1\), \(m = 7\), and these satisfy the second as well, since \(-14 + 5 = -9\). So \(\overrightarrow{c} = 7\overrightarrow{a} - \overrightarrow{b}\), i.e. \(\overrightarrow{c}\) really is a linear combination of \(\overrightarrow{a}\) and \(\overrightarrow{b}\), confirming that the three vectors are coplanar.

**Answer:** \(p = 3\)

\(\overrightarrow{AB} = \left( 0 - 2 \right)\widehat{i} + \left( -1 - 1 \right)\widehat{j} + \left( 0 + 1 \right)\widehat{k} = -2\widehat{i} - 2\widehat{j} + \widehat{k}\)
\(\overrightarrow{AC} = \left( 4 - 2 \right)\widehat{i} + \left( 0 - 1 \right)\widehat{j} + \left( 4 + 1 \right)\widehat{k} = 2\widehat{i} - \widehat{j} + 5\widehat{k}\)
\(\overrightarrow{AD} = \left( 2 - 2 \right)\widehat{i} + \left( 0 - 1 \right)\widehat{j} + \left( 1 + 1 \right)\widehat{k} = 0\widehat{i} - \widehat{j} + 2\widehat{k}\)

First,
\(\overrightarrow{AC} \times \overrightarrow{AD} = \begin{vmatrix} \widehat{i} & \widehat{j} & \widehat{k} \\ 2 & -1 & 5 \\ 0 & -1 & 2 \end{vmatrix} = \widehat{i}\left( (-1)(2) - (5)(-1) \right) - \widehat{j}\left( (2)(2) - (5)(0) \right) + \widehat{k}\left( (2)(-1) - (-1)(0) \right)\)
\(= \widehat{i}(-2 + 5) - \widehat{j}(4 - 0) + \widehat{k}(-2 - 0) = 3\widehat{i} - 4\widehat{j} - 2\widehat{k}\)

Then
\(\left\lbrack \overrightarrow{AB}\ \overrightarrow{AC}\ \overrightarrow{AD} \right\rbrack = \overrightarrow{AB} \cdot \left( \overrightarrow{AC} \times \overrightarrow{AD} \right) = (-2)(3) + (-2)(-4) + (1)(-2)\)
\(= -6 + 8 - 2 = 0\)

Since the scalar triple product is zero, the vectors \(\overrightarrow{AB}\), \(\overrightarrow{AC}\), \(\overrightarrow{AD}\) are coplanar, and all three start at \(A\).

Hence the points \(A(2, 1, -1)\), \(B(0, -1, 0)\), \(C(4, 0, 4)\) and \(D(2, 0, 1)\) are coplanar.

\(\text{Volume} = \dfrac{1}{3} \times \text{base area} \times \text{height}\)

Let \(ABC\) be a triangle, and let \(\overrightarrow{a}\), \(\overrightarrow{b}\), \(\overrightarrow{c}\) be the position vectors of \(A\), \(B\), \(C\) with respect to some origin.

The altitudes from \(A\) and from \(B\) are not parallel (they are perpendicular to the non-parallel sides \(BC\) and \(AC\)), so they meet. Let \(P\left( \overrightarrow{p} \right)\) be their point of intersection.

To prove that all three altitudes are concurrent it is enough to show that the altitude from \(C\) also passes through \(P\), i.e. that \(\overrightarrow{CP} \perp \overrightarrow{AB}\).

Since \(P\) lies on the altitude from \(A\), \(\overrightarrow{AP} \perp \overrightarrow{BC}\):
\(\overrightarrow{AP} \cdot \overrightarrow{BC} = 0\)
\(\therefore \left( \overrightarrow{p} - \overrightarrow{a} \right) \cdot \left( \overrightarrow{c} - \overrightarrow{b} \right) = 0\)
\(\therefore \overrightarrow{p} \cdot \overrightarrow{c} - \overrightarrow{p} \cdot \overrightarrow{b} - \overrightarrow{a} \cdot \overrightarrow{c} + \overrightarrow{a} \cdot \overrightarrow{b} = 0\) ... (1)

Since \(P\) lies on the altitude from \(B\), \(\overrightarrow{BP} \perp \overrightarrow{AC}\):
\(\overrightarrow{BP} \cdot \overrightarrow{AC} = 0\)
\(\therefore \left( \overrightarrow{p} - \overrightarrow{b} \right) \cdot \left( \overrightarrow{c} - \overrightarrow{a} \right) = 0\)
\(\therefore \overrightarrow{p} \cdot \overrightarrow{c} - \overrightarrow{p} \cdot \overrightarrow{a} - \overrightarrow{b} \cdot \overrightarrow{c} + \overrightarrow{b} \cdot \overrightarrow{a} = 0\) ... (2)

Subtract (1) from (2). The terms \(\overrightarrow{p} \cdot \overrightarrow{c}\) cancel, and \(\overrightarrow{a} \cdot \overrightarrow{b} = \overrightarrow{b} \cdot \overrightarrow{a}\) so those cancel too:
\(-\overrightarrow{p} \cdot \overrightarrow{a} + \overrightarrow{p} \cdot \overrightarrow{b} - \overrightarrow{b} \cdot \overrightarrow{c} + \overrightarrow{a} \cdot \overrightarrow{c} = 0\)
\(\therefore \overrightarrow{p} \cdot \left( \overrightarrow{b} - \overrightarrow{a} \right) - \overrightarrow{c} \cdot \left( \overrightarrow{b} - \overrightarrow{a} \right) = 0\)
